{
  "candidate_rtl": "module addr_calcu(
    input [7:0] address,
    input [7:0] ptr1, ptr2,
    input [7:0] b,
    input control,
    output [15:0] count
);

    parameter [7:0] base = 8'b10000000;

    wire [7:0] selected_pointer;
    wire [7:0] inverse_offset;
    wire offset_nonzero;
    wire [7:0] csa_sum;
    wire [7:0] csa_carry;
    wire [9:0] total;
    wire negative_result;

    assign selected_pointer = control ? ptr1 : ptr2;

    // Mandatory modulo-256 arithmetic:
    // inverse_offset = -( (base-selected_pointer) mod 256 ) mod 256.
    // At the default base, this is just an inversion of pointer bit 7.
    assign inverse_offset = selected_pointer - base;
    assign offset_nonzero = |inverse_offset;

    // Compress three unsigned 8-bit operands without carry propagation.
    assign csa_sum = address ^ b ^ inverse_offset;
    assign csa_carry = (address & b) |
                       (address & inverse_offset) |
                       (b & inverse_offset);

    // Exact unsigned sum, in the range 0 through 765.
    assign total = {2'b00, csa_sum} + {1'b0, csa_carry, 1'b0};

    // Subtract 256 precisely when the original truncated offset is nonzero.
    // The mathematical result is in [-255,510], so bits 15:9 agree.
    assign negative_result = offset_nonzero & ~(|total[9:8]);
    assign count = {{7{negative_result}},
                    (total[8] ^ offset_nonzero), total[7:0]};

endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The measured baseline maximum arrival is 2.38 ns, with control-to-count[10:12] paths traversing a buffer and multiple arithmetic-looking logic stages. The verified pre-techmap optimization log establishes that Yosys moved the output selection ahead of shared arithmetic, leaving a potential mux-to-three-ALU dependency chain. This supports investigating arithmetic propagation after selection, rather than merely moving the RTL mux. It does not establish three serial mapped adders or precisely identify individual gates with RTL operators. The final NOR stage alone contributes approximately 0.43 ns on the supplied paths, so upper-output decoding and drive also deserve attention.",
  "rewrite": "Replace the offset subtraction followed by wide subtraction/addition with an equivalent modulo-256 inverse-offset representation. Let q=(selected_pointer-base) mod 256. The original zero-extended offset satisfies -offset=q-256*(q!=0). For default base=128, q requires only inversion of the selected pointer's most significant bit. A bitwise carry-save compressor combines address, b, and q, followed by one explicit 10-bit carry-propagating addition. The subtraction of 256 is implemented directly in the upper-output encoding instead of another wide arithmetic operation. This changes the arithmetic representation rather than relying on duplicated branches surviving synthesis.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Hypothesis, not a measurement: removing the default-instance offset carry propagation and compressing three operands before the final addition should shorten the arithmetic dependency and may reduce maximum arrival below 2.38 ns. No defensible numerical gain is available without running the fixed flow. Selection delay, final carry propagation, replicated upper-bit loading, and ABC restructuring can limit or eliminate the improvement.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The candidate uses one pointer mux, an 8-bit carry-save compressor, a 10-bit final addition, a reduction detector, and small upper-output encoding logic. This is a plausible area reduction relative to the baseline's shared arithmetic, but mapped area is unmeasured. The replicated upper-output signal and reduction detector may require buffering or upsizing. Acceptance requires mapped area no greater than 1311.632960 um^2, full formal equivalence, and zero max-slew and max-capacitance violations under the specified flow; none of those candidate checks has been performed here.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The module name, ports, widths, and parameter declaration/default are preserved. All 33 ordinary input bits remain unconstrained, with control selecting ptr1 when high and ptr2 otherwise. The 8-bit assignment to inverse_offset explicitly preserves modulo-256 truncation; it is not an untruncated substitution for the original offset. If q is zero, the original offset is zero; otherwise the original offset is 256-q. Thus the mathematical result is total-256*(q!=0), ranging from -255 through 510. Its low byte is total[7:0], bit 8 is total[8] XOR (q!=0), and bits 15:9 are all the negative-result indicator. These identities preserve modulo-65536 behavior. The algebra also applies to other 8-bit base values, although only the default instance is assessed and receives the trivial inverse-offset hardware. No clocks, state, assumptions, or don't-cares are introduced."
}
